# the-internet-herokuapp-com-cypress-tests

A Cypress + TypeScript test suite for https://the-internet.herokuapp.com, generated by
[Suite Builder](https://github.com/Ghost-in-the-Kernel-Labs/Ghost-in-the-Kernel-Labs-suite-builder-docs) from a crawl of the site. Its pages and the links between them: [SITE-GRAPH.md](SITE-GRAPH.md).

## Run it

**Lost? Type `crew` in this folder** (or `help`, `suite`, `ask`; in PowerShell `.\crew`, on a Mac or Linux `./crew`): where the suite stands, and a menu of what to do, Claude Code's help among it.

**Rather click than type? `crew`, then "Open the test library"** (or `node menu/library.mjs`): every family and test on one page, on this computer only; click one and watch it run. "Put the test library on the desktop" in the same menu sets it up once for someone who never opens a terminal: an icon they double-click. "Get the team's latest" (page and menu) brings in what the team pushed to the suite's repository, never overwriting a change made on this computer.

**Stories in Jira? Type `jira login` here, once**: then `jira pull` brings the ready stories in and `jira push` sends each card its tests or its questions. `jira-loop/README.md` explains it, for the BA too.

Needs Node 20+. From this folder, once: `npm ci` (exactly the packages `package-lock.json` holds, with no package's install script run: `.npmrc`), then `npx cypress install` (the Cypress app, several hundred MB: minutes). Then:

```
npm run smoke                every page type loads (start here)
npm test                     the suite's rules, then every test, headless
npm run navigation           header, footer and page links land on the right pages
npm run links                every address the crawl requested, asked again: cypress/link-report.md
                             (fails on one broken since the crawl; 9 broken then, listed)
                             and the 7 links to other sites: cypress/external-link-report.md
npm run stories              the story tests
npm run critical             the critical family: what matters most, marked by you
npm run family -- checkout   any family, yours included (cypress/families.txt)
npm run open                 Cypress's own window: watch each test, step by step
npm test -- --browser firefox            in Firefox (or edge, electron); Chrome by default, Electron without it
BASE_URL=https://staging.example.com npm test     against another copy of the site
npx cypress run --expose blockAds=false  with ads (blocked by default: they hijack clicks; for every
                                         run, expose: { blockAds: false } in cypress.config.ts's YOURS settings)
npx cypress run --expose testDelay=1000  a second between tests, on a site you don't own (for every run,
                                         expose: { testDelay: 1000 } in cypress.config.ts's YOURS settings)
npx cypress run --expose stopAfter=0     every test, even after 5 in a row fail the same way (the run
                                         stops early then, by default, the rest skipped, saying why)
npx cypress run --expose loadBudget=2.5  fail a test whose page takes over 2.5 s to be ready (every page is
                                         timed anyway: cypress/timings/timings.csv, the slowest listed at the end)
npx cypress run --expose apiBudget=1.5   fail an API call that takes over 1.5 s (every call is timed anyway:
                                         cypress/timings/api.csv, the slowest and the slow ones listed at the end)
```

**API tests.** `support/core/Api.ts` is ready: `Api.site().get('/api/products').then((a) => Api.expect(a).status(200).json('items[0].name', 'Lamp'))`;
`.asRole('user')` signs a call in with that role's account (read in Node, never logged), `.bearer(token)` with a
token; each call is a step in the test's log. When the crawl read the site's API document (a Swagger UI or ReDoc page),
`cypress/e2e/cases/api.cy.ts` asks each operation a test can call as it is, held to what the document says it answers:
`npm run api`.

**Test families.** smoke, critical, navigation, links, stories, api, and any of your own: a test joins one by
its options, `it('...', { tags: ['smoke'] }, () => { ... })`, or a `describe`'s, and `npm run family --
smoke` runs every test of it, in any spec. A family of your own: a line in `cypress/families.txt`'s YOURS
block, then `npm run family -- <its name>`; a name not declared there is refused, not run empty.

Every test starts with no cookies. Each prints its steps in plain English as it takes them
(`   3. Click "Careers" in the header`); a failed one says which step failed, and why, and leaves its
evidence in `cypress/failures/<spec>/<test>/` (steps.txt, page.html, console.txt) with its
screenshot in `cypress/screenshots/`. `npm test` checks the suite's rules first (SUITE-RULES.md);
a broken rule says where, why the rule exists and what to change. The tests run whatever it says: a
broken hard or story rule fails the run at the end, an advisory one is a warning (cypress/rules-report.md).
A page gets 30 seconds to load and a check 10.

What Cypress does differently from the Java suites: it drives one tab, so a link that opens a new
tab is followed in the same one; and a dropdown that opens on CSS `:hover` alone can't be opened
(Cypress has no real mouse), so its links are clicked where they are. Both still check where the link
leads.

## In a pipeline

GitHub, GitLab and Azure: `.github/workflows/suite.yml`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `azure-pipelines.yml` (keep yours): the
quick check (http and smoke) on every push, every test nightly in chromium and firefox. The `Dockerfile` runs the suite anywhere.
Delete the ones you don't use: a rebuild leaves them out (an empty file of the same name brings one back).

## What's here

```
cypress/support/core/     LoadablePage, WaitActions, UserActions, Checks, Find, StepLog, CookieBanner, SiteConfig, ...
cypress/support/uri/      UrlPaths: every page's path
cypress/support/pages/    one folder per page type, e.g. home/:
  HomePage.ts            open(), isLoaded(): URL, full page load, title, key elements
  HomeElements.ts        locators: section headings, links, a marked place for your own
  HomeTasks.ts           a form's task, filled and not sent (a page with a form)
  actions/                a class per door the page has: HomeReadActions, ...VerifyActions, and ...ClickActions,
                          ...EnterActions, ...CheckActions when it has links or buttons, fields, checkboxes
cypress/e2e/cases/        the tests: smoke, navigation, menus, the link report, and your stories
cypress/e2e/harness.cy.ts the harness testing itself (with every run)
suite-rules/              the suite's rules (check.mjs) and fingerprints
```

## Editing, and regenerating

Every file says in its first lines what may be edited. Most are generated with **YOURS** blocks;
regenerating (`suite build the-internet-herokuapp-com-cypress-tests`) rewrites everything else and keeps what is in the blocks.
Work that no longer has a place is moved to `orphaned/`, never deleted. Files that are wholly yours
(package.json, CHANGES.md, cypress/support/smoke-overrides.ts, your story tests) are never touched.

Two blocks start with what the crawl found, for you to change: each page class's `PROVES_LOADED`
(what proves it has loaded: take out a heading that comes and goes) and a family's `EXAMPLES` (the
pages `open()` and the smoke test use). Left as they are, a rebuild brings the newer crawl's
versions; changed, yours are kept. To replace a smoke test, give your version in
`cypress/support/smoke-overrides.ts` under the test's name (it lists them): it runs instead.

## Write a test

The worked example in this suite is `cypress/e2e/cases/two-factor-form.cy.ts`, a test of TwoFactorPage, chosen because its form has the fewest fields of any page's. Open it beside `cypress/support/pages/twofactor/`: it opens TwoFactorPage, checks the browser will not send its form empty, fills it through `execute().fillLogInWithTomsmithAndSuperSecretPa1iaczzvForm(...)` with test data you can change, and checks each field holds what was typed. Nothing is sent: what happens after Send is the one thing left, and its YOURS block shows the lines to add.

A spec of your own in `cypress/e2e/cases/` with plain `it()` tests is held to one rule: each test
checks something (SUITE-RULES.md).

```ts
import { HomePage } from '../../support/pages/home/HomePage';

it('the home page opens', () => {
  new HomePage().open().verify().isLoaded();
});
```

A test that comes from a story in your tracker is better written as a story (`story()`):
ai/AI-README.md says how.

## Working with an AI

With [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), signed in with your own account, run `claude` in this
folder, then:

- `/stories`: the stories in stories/new/ become tests, or come back saying exactly what is needed;
- `/fix-failing`: the last run's failed tests read, the suite's faults fixed, the site's recorded in KNOWN-ISSUES.md;
- `/explain-audit`: the site's audit, explained for its owner, the most serious first.

`ai/AI-README.md` is written for an AI assistant: hand it this folder, put the stories in stories/new/, and
say "do the stories". The crawl this was generated from is in `crawl/`: keep it with the project.
